events.title: Kepler's Supernova Lights Up the Sky
events.description: Astronomers across Europe noticed a dazzlingly bright new star in the constellation Ophiuchus in early October 1604. Johannes Kepler studied it closely and wrote a celebrated account of it. It remains the most recent supernova seen with the naked eye in our Milky Way galaxy.
events.significance: The event challenged the old idea that the heavens never change, and it is still the last supernova visible to the naked eye in our galaxy.

events.title: Washington Monument Opens to the Public
events.description: After decades of delays, including a pause caused by the Civil War and a shortage of funds, the Washington Monument opened to visitors. It was the tallest structure in the world at the time. Early visitors could ride a steam-powered elevator to the top.
events.significance: The monument honors George Washington and became a defining landmark of the National Mall and the American capital.

events.title: John Lennon Is Born in Liverpool
events.description: John Winston Lennon was born in Liverpool, England. He co-founded the Beatles and wrote many of their best-known songs with Paul McCartney. He later became a solo artist and peace activist.
events.significance: Lennon helped reshape popular music and youth culture in the 1960s, and his songwriting still influences artists today.

events.title: Uganda Gains Independence
events.description: Uganda became independent from British rule and joined the Commonwealth as a sovereign nation. The date is still celebrated each year as Independence Day.
events.significance: Uganda's independence was part of the wave of African decolonization that transformed the continent in the early 1960s.

events.title: Che Guevara Is Executed in Bolivia
events.description: A day after being captured by Bolivian forces, the Argentine-born revolutionary Ernesto "Che" Guevara was executed in the village of La Higuera. He had been trying to start a guerrilla uprising in Bolivia.
events.significance: His death ended his final campaign, and his image has since become one of the most widely reproduced symbols of rebellion in the world.
